title: The Perihelion Run
subtitle: Eleven Hours in the Shadow of a Ship, and the Sun Does Not Negotiate

listing.title: The Perihelion Run ☀️
listing.blurb: Steal Lot Zero from the pleasure liner Aubade during the eleven hours it dives past the sun, deaf, blind and cut off from the rest of the system. The cargo turns out to be a woman, she is the one flying the ship, and she has her own opinion about who gets to own her. Levels 4–9.

synopsis: Once a year the Ostrander Line's flagship, the pleasure liner Aubade, leaves Caloris High above Mercury with two thousand two hundred very rich passengers and dives to within four million kilometres of the sun for the Perihelion Gala: eleven hours with the star filling the sky, champagne in the Orangery and the most expensive sunrise in the system. For those eleven hours, called the Glare, the Aubade lives entirely in the shadow of its own heat shield, the Parasol. Its sensor mast is folded away behind it, its point-defence is stowed because it would melt, its docking fields are cycled down, and solar noise kills every signal in or out. Nobody can call for help and nobody can come. You are a crew of hired contractors brought together by a fixer named Oriel Mabb on behalf of Sarrow Cognitive. The job: during the Glare, take Lot Zero out of the Aubade's vault, the Reliquary, before the Line sells it at the Gala to Kessane Armaments, then get clear in the hour between the sun letting go of you and the ship's sensors coming back. Lot Zero is listed as a prototype navigation lattice. It is not. It is Isaura Vell, the engineer who designed the Aubade's sun-dive, uploaded the day she died nine years ago and kept since then as Line property. She has flown every perihelion pass since, from a cradle in the Reliquary, and the Ostrander Line has never told the captain. When you lift her out of that cradle the ship starts to drift, the shadow starts to shrink, and your own ship is waiting inside it. She does not want to be sold to Kessane. She does not want to be stolen by Sarrow either. She will negotiate, and she has eleven hours too.
hook: The message comes on a burn-after-read chit with a Caloris High dock number and a time. Oriel Mabb meets you in a noodle bar under the quay's radiator fins, where everything smells of coolant and soy. She is small, neat and very polite, and she slides a holo across the table of a ship most of the system has only seen on advertising: the Aubade, fourteen hundred metres of white hull and gold glass, with a heat shield like a lily pad stuck on the front. 'Thirty hours from now she leaves on the Gala run,' Mabb says. 'Eleven hours after that she is the most isolated object in the inner system. No comms, no sensors, no help. In her vault there is an item the Line calls Lot Zero, which my client would rather Kessane Armaments did not own. Sixty thousand credits each, half when you come aboard and half on delivery. The ship that takes you in has to stay in the liner's shadow the whole time or it burns, and it can only get out in one hour of the eleven. The sun is the deadline, and you can't talk a sun into anything.' She smiles. 'I'll want your answer before the noodles come.'

setting.name: The SLV Aubade and the Glare
setting.description: The inner system, a long way into the future. Mercury is a mining world wrapped in solar collectors and radiator fins. Its orbital port, Caloris High, is the jumping-off point for sun-skimmer refineries, research stations and the rich. The Aubade is the Ostrander Line's last great ship and the last asset of a family that has been losing money for twenty years. She is a 1,400-metre pleasure liner carrying 2,200 passengers and 900 crew, built as a long spindle. At the bow is the Parasol, a 600-metre sunward heat shield with a ceramic face, mounted on articulated roots. Behind it come the bridge, the gold-glass Promenade and the Orangery gala decks, the passenger towers and the zero-g keel called the Spine, which runs the full length of the ship. Below the Spine and well shadowed, near the stern, sits the Reliquary, the Line's vault. The annual Perihelion Gala dives to six solar radii. For the eleven hours of closest approach the ship's survival depends on keeping the Parasol aimed at the sun to within a tenth of a degree, a feat the brochures credit to 'the Vell Engine, our proprietary navigation lattice'. That is the truth stated in a way designed to hide it.
setting.atmosphere: Gold light, white hull, black shadow. Luxury pressed right up against lethality. Champagne and string quartets on one side of a bulkhead, and on the other a coolant line, a pressure door and a few metres of ceramic between you and a star. Everyone aboard is very rich, very bored or working, and every passenger in the Orangery is looking out of a window that would kill them in a second if the Parasol slipped. Play it as a heist first: plans, covers, crew banter, the pleasure of competent people doing something difficult. Then let the job go wrong in physical, mechanical ways a crew can fight. The clock is real, gunfire has consequences, and vacuum doesn't care how good your plan was. The cargo is a person. Do not play her as a voice in a box. She is the cleverest person aboard and has been bored, lonely and furious for nine years.

regions.name: Caloris High
regions.description: Mercury's orbital port, a ring of docks and refineries shaded by kilometre-long radiator fins. Noodle bars, customs officers, fixers and cheap ship berths. The crew plans here and the Aubade departs from here at T-30.

regions.name: The Promenade and the Orangery
regions.description: The Aubade's gala decks under gold glass: the Promenade arcade, the Orangery ballroom with real orange trees, the Lantern Bar and the auction salon where Lot Zero will be sold at G+8. Passengers, stewards, bodyguards, cameras and Gala security.

regions.name: The Spine
regions.description: The zero-g keel that runs the length of the ship: freight tubes, coolant trunks, cable runs, maintenance crawlways and the drone galleries. It is dim, cold and loud, and the fastest route from bow to stern for anyone who can move without gravity.

regions.name: The Reliquary
regions.description: The Ostrander vault, deep in the shadowed stern keel: a strongroom of family treasures and, behind a second door, the cradle chamber where Lot Zero is kept. It is cold, quiet and very heavily guarded, and it sits against the outer hull.

regions.name: The Parasol and the Shadow
regions.description: The heat shield and the cone of shadow behind it, 600 metres wide at the bow and narrowing to a few hundred metres past the stern. Inside the cone a ship can survive. Outside it, during the Glare, nothing survives.

regions.name: The Pale Moth
regions.description: The crew's ship, a 40-metre refitted sun-skimmer tender with ablative skirts, grapples and far too many patches. She rides the Aubade's shadow under her stern. She is the way in, the way out and, if the shadow shrinks, the first thing to burn.

campaignRules.name: The Clock
campaignRules.description: The campaign runs on two published clocks. The GM states the time at the start of every scene and whenever it changes, and never fudges it. T-MINUS counts down from departure at Caloris High (T-30) to the start of the Glare (T-0). THE GLARE runs G+0 to G+11. At G+0 the Parasol locks into perihelion attitude, comms and long-range sensors die, the sensor mast folds and the point-defence stows. At G+8 the Lot Zero auction opens in the Orangery salon. At G+10 the solar flux outside the shadow drops enough that the Pale Moth's ablative skirts will survive about 20 minutes in sunlight. At G+11 the shields close: the mast deploys, sensors and comms come back, docking fields come up, point-defence goes live and the Line's armed escort cutter Clemency picks up anything within 10,000 km. The escape window is G+10 to G+11 and nothing the crew does can move it. Time costs: a short rest takes 1 hour, a careful Jury-Rig or vault stage 10-30 minutes, a fight 1 minute plus the aftermath, and travelling the Spine from bow to stern 20 minutes (10 for a Spacer or anyone with Zero-G Adapted). If the crew is still aboard at G+11 the run is not over, but it becomes a different and much worse kind of job (see ph-scenario-004).

campaignRules.name: The Shadow
campaignRules.description: During the Glare, anything outside the Parasol's shadow cone takes 10d10 fire damage per round, plus 1d10 radiant per round to electronics and Synthetics, and unshielded vacuum suits fail in 1 round. Only the Pale Moth's ablative skirts survive sunlight, and only after G+10, for about 20 minutes. The cone's edge, the terminator, is visible on the hull as a ruled line between white-hot and black. The cone keeps its shape only while the ship holds attitude. Each 10 minutes the Aubade spends without a competent pilot-mind (see Lot Zero in ph-scenario-003), the ship drifts and the terminator moves 20 metres along the stern hull. The GM tracks this as a number on the table: Drift 0 to 10. At Drift 4 the stern hull plating starts to ablate and the Moth must move. At Drift 7 the Reliquary's outer wall is in sunlight. At Drift 10 the Parasol root fails and the Aubade is lost with everyone aboard. Drift drops by 1 for every 10 minutes the ship is flown well.

campaignRules.name: Hull Breach & Decompression
campaignRules.description: The Aubade is a pressurised ship and gunfire aboard her has consequences. Weapons are hull hazards in three classes. SHIP-SAFE: frangible ballistic rounds, stun and arc weapons, and lasers on standard cells. These never breach a pressure hull, although a laser can still crack a viewport on a natural 1. HULL HAZARD: standard ballistic rounds, plasma and explosives. Any miss by 5 or more, or any natural 1, when the line of fire runs toward an exterior wall, viewport or Spine trunk breaches it on a d6 roll of 1-3, and an explosive in contact with a hull always breaches. HULL BREAKER: rail weapons and heavy weapons. Any hit or miss that overpenetrates breaches on a d6 roll of 1-5. WHEN A BREACH OPENS: the compartment decompresses explosively. Every creature within 30 ft makes a DC 15 Strength or Dexterity save (its choice) or is pulled 20 ft toward the breach. A creature that fails by 5 or more while within 10 ft of a breach larger than a hand is blown out. Loose objects become hazards (1d6 bludgeoning to everyone within 10 ft of the breach line). Emergency bulkheads seal the compartment at the end of the 1d4th round unless someone holds them open or overrides them (Computers DC 15). VACUUM: a creature without a sealed suit can act for a number of rounds equal to 1 + its CON modifier (minimum 1), after which it drops to 0 HP and is dying. Synthetics do not breathe but take 1d6 cold damage per minute in vacuum. SEALING: patching a hand-sized breach takes an action and sealant foam (Mechanics DC 12). A body-sized breach needs a patch plate and three rounds (Mechanics DC 15). The ship's own response to a breach always adds 1 Heat.

campaignRules.name: Zero-G
campaignRules.description: The Spine, the freight tubes, the drone galleries and anything outside the hull are microgravity. Movement: you move by pushing off a surface and travel in a straight line at up to double speed, but you cannot change direction until you reach a surface or handhold. Stopping without one takes an Acrobatics check (DC 12) or you hit the next surface and take 1d6 bludgeoning. Combat: a creature not braced against a surface or handhold has disadvantage on melee attacks. Firing a ballistic or plasma weapon unbraced pushes you 10 ft directly away from your target (an Athletics or Acrobatics check, DC 10 for Sidearms or 15 for anything bigger, holds you still). Lasers and stun weapons have no recoil. Grappling in zero-g: a creature that grapples an unbraced creature can move it freely. Spacers and anyone with Zero-G Adapted ignore all of these penalties and are the most dangerous people in the Spine. Mag-boots let anyone walk on a surface at normal speed and count as braced, but you cannot push off while they are clamped.

campaignRules.name: Heat
campaignRules.description: Heat measures how much the Aubade knows something is wrong and how badly it wants to find out what. It is one shared track for the crew, 0 to 10, shown openly. It goes up by 1 for: a blown cover, an alarm tripped (any Computers check failed by 5 or more), a guard who doesn't check in, unsuppressed gunfire anywhere in a passenger section, a breach, or a drone destroyed where another can see the wreck. It goes up by 2 for a body found or a passenger hurt. It goes down by 1 for every 2 hours with no incident, or through a cover story that holds (Deception or Persuasion against the investigating officer). THRESHOLDS. Heat 3: Commander Varga-Thorn doubles patrols and security drones (Wardens) start random identity checks; disadvantage on Stealth in public areas. Heat 6: lockdown. Pressure doors between sections need security codes, Warden drones hunt in pairs and the Reliquary garrison doubles. Heat 9: Varga-Thorn is authorised to vent compartments to atmosphere to stop intruders. She will not do it near passengers, but she will do it in the Spine and the Reliquary, and she will say so first on the open channel. Heat never drops below 6 once anyone has opened the Reliquary.

campaignRules.name: Her Regard
campaignRules.description: Isaura Vell, Lot Zero, has a Regard for the crew from -3 to +3. It starts at 0 when she first speaks (ph-scenario-003) and the GM tracks it privately but plays it openly. It goes up when the crew treats her as a person with a vote: asking rather than telling, being honest about who hired them, keeping a promise, protecting passengers. It goes down when they handle her as cargo, lie to her (she has read every file on this ship and will usually know), threaten to copy her, or let Oriel's kill-key near her. Isaura controls navigation, attitude, the Parasol, and any door, light, speaker or Warden drone wired to the attitude-control net, which covers about a third of the ship including the Spine and the Reliquary. At +2 or higher she opens doors, blinds cameras and flies the ship out of trouble for the crew. At 0 she does exactly what she agreed to and nothing more. At -2 or lower she works against them, carefully and cleverly, and she never risks the passengers to do it.

campaignRules.name: Ship-Safe Arms & Boarding
campaignRules.description: The Aubade scans everything that comes aboard at Caloris High. Energy cells above holdout size, standard ballistic ammunition and explosives are confiscated or flagged, and the Pale Moth has to bring the heavy kit in during the Glare. Smuggling a weapon aboard in the passenger stream is a contested Sleight of Hand or Deception check against the gate scanner team's Perception (+4), or a Mechanics check (DC 15) to disguise it as luggage hardware. Failure means the item is confiscated and Heat starts at 1. The Aubade's own security carry stun pistols, arc batons and frangible-round sidearms. Kessane's auditors carry plasma, because they don't care.

wildernessStarts.label: Caloris High, the noodle bar under the fins
Aboard the Pale Moth, in the shadow

explorationRules: The Perihelion Run is one ship and about forty hours, so exploration means moving through a vertical, guarded, partly weightless building that is diving at a star. The party never travels in the ordinary sense. It splits: the inside team boards at Caloris High under cover (steward, guest, performer, contractor), and the outside team rides the Pale Moth into the shadow at G+0. Run both halves and cut between them like a heist film. Keep scenes short, end each cut on a decision and always state the clock. Encourage the players to make a plan in ph-scenario-001, and let it work when it is good. The fun of a heist is watching a good plan meet a real problem, not watching the GM tear a plan up out of spite. The real problems are already written into the scenarios: Lot Zero is a person, Kessane arrives early, Oriel has a kill-key and the shadow shrinks. Let those do the damage. Movement between areas: Promenade to Spine 5 minutes via a service lift, Spine bow to stern 20 minutes (10 for a Spacer), Spine to Reliquary 5 minutes, Reliquary to Shadow Lock 9 another 5. Moving between decks inside a passenger tower is trivial. Getting past a pressure door at Heat 6 is not.
